title: Verbalised logo and text combination

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines

slide_intent: Express the city’s relationship to an organization so a signature distinguishes ownership, partnership and support.
strategic_value: Consistent wording can make Helsinki’s different civic relationships more understandable without introducing new logos.
demonstration: This expanded webpage section explains three relationship phrases and their language availability, shows Finnish horizontal examples, then compares clear space around horizontal and vertical combinations.
practical_value: Choose the wording from the organization’s relationship to the city before choosing its layout.

content_islands.name: Relationship choices
content_islands.spec: Present With love from, Together with and Supported by Helsinki with their intended users.

content_islands.name: Finnish combinations
content_islands.spec: Stack three horizontal Finnish phrase-and-logo specimens beneath the relationship guidance.

content_islands.name: Space and orientation
content_islands.spec: Follow placement guidance with horizontal and vertical two-H-height clear-space diagrams.

ingredient.name: Verbal framed-logo combinations
ingredient.role: Explain the city’s relationship to the named activity.
ingredient.application: Use With love from for the described foundation-managed cultural/leisure brands, Together with for shared-ownership or strategic partners, and Supported by for grant recipients.
ingredient.scope: Use the language corresponding to the material and preserve two H heights of clear space. Horizontal/right-edge and vertical/top-or-bottom placement are stated suitability guidance.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text says the three variants depend on Helsinki’s operational role or brand relationship.
reference_purposes.Application: The diagrams compare clear space for horizontal and vertical combinations; accompanying text describes suitable edge placements.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Original files and two-H-height protected areas must be used.
